body:
This is great [@Shankar Warang](/edgeware/account/jA7pLH65zgRNA4UgwqHEWWRxTgg51wuAUgfzmZoYWM2dMVS) - great work. 

The idea of bootsrapping our chain factory model via convertible notes that are effectively chain treasury backed feels like an elegant and simple solution to the problem of getting projects started. 

A few thoughts:

- These don't need to be USD / fiat denominated, for instance we're working on a version of this called 'stake-notes' for Kabocha that are initially denominated in KSM and can be used for our year 2 crowdloan and also expand the Seeds idea since the NFT is effectively the note. 


- These can also work well for external groups of investors, institutions or listed companies to purchase - they're effectively treasury bonds issued by our _sovereign network societies_.


- I think the Edgeware snapshot / airdrop model may be a one off for Kabocha, it doesn't make sense to keep duplicating the same distribution and we can more effectively drive participation and value capture with new mechanism designs for the incubated chains / relays that follow. 


- Following on from that point, I think like all these things, we need a very simple implementation of this idea in the first instance, there are too many variables at play in this initial example, let's just reduce to the simplest possible version and see how that works. Complex systems will emerge from very simple ones...   


> For contributors with no public presence in Edgeverse or across social media, they will need to go through a KYC verification process.

- I'd lose this, keep it simple, it's the same as proposals / bounties, anyone can propose, doesn't mean it will pass, putting forward a convertible note should be the same and rely on governance, community veto/approval rather than gatekeeping. Of course this is again where established community members can vouch / propose on behalf of less well known using the network services model, taking some upside on the note but risking downside

This is great [@Shankar Warang](/edgeware/account/jA7pLH65zgRNA4UgwqHEWWRxTgg51wuAUgfzmZoYWM2dMVS) - great work. 

The idea of bootsrapping our chain factory model via convertible notes that are effectively chain treasury backed feels like an elegant and simple solution to the problem of getting projects started. 

A few thoughts:

- These don't need to be USD / fiat denominated, for instance we're working on a version of this called 'stake-notes' for Kabocha that are denominated in KSM. 


- These can also work well for external groups of investors, institutions or listed companies to purchase - they're effectively treasury bonds issued by our _sovereign network societies_.


- I think the Edgeware snapshot / airdrop model may be a one off for Kabocha, it doesn't make sense to keep duplicating the same distribution and we can more effectively drive participation and value capture with new mechanism designs for the incubated chains / relays that follow. 


- Following on from that point, I think like all these things, we need a very simple implementation of this idea in the first instance, there are too many variables at play in this initial example, let's just reduce to the simplest possible version and see how that works. Complex systems will emerge from very simple ones...   


> For contributors with no public presence in Edgeverse or across social media, they will need to go through a KYC verification process.

- I'd lose this, keep it simple, it's the same as proposals / bounties, anyone can propose, doesn't mean it will pass, putting forward a convertible note should be the same and rely on governance, community veto/approval rather than gatekeeping. Of course this is again where established community members can vouch / propose on behalf of less well known using the network services model, taking some upside on the note but risking downside if the request fails. 


- In general the 30% / Supplementary Grants is a nice idea, I think we can simplify though. There is no guarantee new projects will be modelled like Kabocha, so ideally i'd focus on getting this model to work even if the projects are presented differently...
